checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in TX
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
Panel schedule showing existing and proposed circuits
Wire gauge and breaker size for each new circuit
Electrical diagram or one-line drawing (required for panel upgrades)
Utility disconnect location marked on plans

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: No permit is typically required for this exact finish-only scope. If the job expands into plumbing, electrical, or structural work, the appropriate licensed trade contractor pulls the permit on the homeowner's behalf and their license number appears on the application. Owner-builder status does not eliminate permit requirements for regulated trade work.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to Austin Development Services Department (DSD)

response_body.job_summary: paint with no plumbing, electrical, wall removal, layout change, or structural work. In Austin, TX this scope typically does not trigger a building permit if you are only swapping finishes and cabinets in the same footprint and not altering any MEP systems. If countertop replacement requires sink removal/reinstall or any plumbing/electrical changes, separate trade permits would be triggered.
pro_tips: Keep the scope locked: same cabinet footprint, same countertop footprint, no sink move, no appliance relocation, no electrical changes — that is what keeps this out of permit territory
If you later discover a sink or dishwasher needs to move, stop and pull the plumbing/electrical permit before demo
Austin DSD is appointment-only for permit submittals, so if the scope changes, book ahead instead of walking in
Austin requires wet stamps on structural drawings, but that does not apply to this finish-only job unless you add structural work
